notes: Non-discriminating: eval 2 boundary assertions (suspension owner, Pricing, Payouts, Billing, rounds, approval) and most eval 3 findings pass for both configs - the simulated expert's answers carry the baseline there. They need harder, outcome-level assertions (e.g. internal links C/S+ACL instead of Conformist; unconfirmed relationships confirmed, not relabelled).

Discriminating: heuristic order, read-back, critic use, one-question-per-context, discovery report and canvases (eval 1: 10/10 vs 4/10). In eval 2 the baseline map made every internal downstream Conformist - not caught by any mechanical assertion.

Cost: with-skill is ~2.3x tokens and ~3x time on average (eval 2: 255k tokens / 20 min vs 79k / 4 min). Token counts exclude nested critic and expert subagents, so the real gap is larger. Eval 3 spent 13 critic calls, all AGREE in round 1, none changed a relationship.
Weakness found: eval 2 with-skill kept an indirect U/D cycle with a justification instead of trying to flip a link (the baseline broke the same loop by letting the called context offer an API).

Eval-harness artifact: concurrent runs shared the session scratchpad; eval 1 with-skill transcript message 1 was overwritten (the real message is reflected in discovery.md and the expert reply). Single run per config, so no variance estimate.
